title: Scripture: no one is without sin—so some sins coexist with true holiness
source_text: IX. Quae certe ex Scripturis sacris evidenter colliguntur. Nam Scriptura sacra docet multis in locis neminem sine peccato vivere. Ut quum dicit Jacobus, In multis offendimus omnes. Et Salomon in Ecclesiaste, Non est homo justus in terra, qui faciat bonum, & non peccet. Et Joannes similiter, Si dixerimus nos peccatum non habere, nos ipsos seducimus, & veritas in nobis non est. Unde necessario sequitur, cum fideles nulli, quantumlibet pii & justitiae studentes, sine peccatis in hac vita degant, quaedam esse peccata quae cum vera justitia & sanctitate simul stent, & cum quibus servare liceat bonam conscientiam, eaque dona & fructus Spiritus, quae piorum in hac vita propria esse Scriptura declarat. Jac. 3. Eccl. 7. 1 Joan. 1.
pass_a_gloss: Which things are certainly gathered evidently from the holy Scriptures. For holy Scripture teaches in many places that no one lives without sin. As when James says, In many things we all offend. And Solomon in Ecclesiastes, There is not a just man upon earth that does good and does not sin. And John likewise, If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. Whence it necessarily follows that, since no believers, however godly and zealous for righteousness, live without sins in this life, there are certain sins which stand together with true righteousness and holiness, and with which it is lawful to keep a good conscience and those gifts and fruits of the Spirit which Scripture declares to be proper to the godly in this life. James 3. Eccl. 7. 1 John 1.
pass_b_english: James, Ecclesiastes, and 1 John prove no believer lives sinless.
Therefore some sins must coexist with true holiness, a good conscience, and the Spirit’s fruits.

choices.why: Logical hinge from universal sinfulness to compatible lighter sins.
